title: Product of Array Except Self
description:
Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` is equal to the product of all the elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`.

The product of any prefix or suffix of `nums` is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit signed integer.

You must write an algorithm that runs in `O(n)` time and without using the division operation. For space complexity analysis, the output array does not count as extra space.
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit signed integer.
hints: For each index i, the product of all elements except nums[i] equals (product of elements strictly to the left of i) * (product of elements strictly to the right of i).
Compute the prefix products in a left-to-right pass directly into the output array.
Then sweep right-to-left while maintaining a single scalar suffix product and multiply it into the output array for O(1) extra space.

examples.explanation: Only index 2 (where nums[2] == 0) has a non-zero product: (-1) * 1 * (-3) * 3 = 9; all other positions include 0 in their product.
